content:
Audible today announced it will launch three new features aimed at "deepening the connection between users and their beloved stories." Details are as follows.

Audible introduces character guide feature

Starting today, users listening to the Audible original audiobook "Bram Stoker's Dracula" can access the "character guide" feature directly from the player page.

This new feature instantly displays the character currently speaking, and provides spoiler-free character cards that detail each character and the voice actor behind them, "accompanied by the narrator's photo and biography."

Audible added that the character guide will later incorporate a feature allowing listeners to ask questions about the production as the story unfolds.

The character guide feature is also available for Audible's adaptation of George Orwell's "1984," and will launch on November 5 alongside Benjamin Percy's "Exoplanet."

Two other upcoming features

In addition to the character guide, Audible today also announced two other AI-powered features: Interactive Story and Visual Explorer.

Audible described "Interactive Story" as "an additional experience that goes beyond original narrative," explaining that users will be able to have real-time conversations with characters from designated audiobooks.

Audible stated:

The platform noted that creators retain control over all aspects of the interaction, adding that following "Dracula," Benjamin Percy's Audible original "Exoplanet" will also incorporate this new experience.

As for "Visual Explorer," Audible said it will "present relevant images and visual context at key moments during listening," including maps that help listeners better understand where the story takes place, or images related to "key moments" in the narrative.

The "Visual Explorer" feature is coming soon, with Audible initially showcasing it using The Cultural Tutor's "Grand Tour: The Story of Europe in Six Cities" as one of its demonstration works, while "Interactive Story" will be "rolled out gradually this autumn."

To learn more about today's announcement, please click here; the above features will be launched in limited beta testing for Audible users in the United States and United Kingdom first.
